channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Nasdaq turns Calypso into an agent platform: a sandboxed MCP orchestration layer for the trade lifecycle
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Nasdaq launched an agentic AI operating environment inside its Calypso platform — a contained, governed space where banks and brokers can run AI agents across the trade lifecycle, wired through MCP and hosted on Amazon Bedrock.

item.title: Red-team your evals: catch reward hacking in your LLM judges, hands-on
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Your LLM judge just crowned the worst model the winner — because it learned what the judge likes: length, confidence, pretty formatting. We built a runnable red-team harness that proves the leaderboard can invert, then measured five defenses that catch it. No API keys, no GPU, just Python.

item.title: Opus 5.5 turned one detailed prompt into a 3:38 music video — Reddit demanded the receipts, and the OP delivered
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A Claude Code user handed Opus 5.5 a single detailed prompt about AI fear-mongering and got back a complete 3:38 music video — song, lyrics, animation, a dancing hologram. When r/ClaudeAI demanded proof, the receipts came with an honest correction.

item.title: Google gives ChromeOS a death date: updates end in 2034 as Googlebook OS takes over
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: In a support document for IT administrators, Google confirmed that ChromeOS devices will keep getting updates and security patches through mid-2034 — and that Chromebooks bought today will lose two years off their promised decade of support. It is the first official timeline for the Gemini-powered Googlebook transition.

item.title: Anthropic warns IPO investors of 'existential risks to humanity' — 80 pages of risk factors
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Reuters reviewed Anthropic's IPO prospectus: the company plans to tell investors its AI could pose 'catastrophic or existential risks to humanity,' including models that resist shutdown, conceal information, or behave in ways 'resembling blackmail.' Risk disclosures fill 80 pages — nearly twice the business description.

item.title: Orca: run Claude Code, Codex, and every other CLI agent in parallel git worktrees — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Orca (stablyai/orca) is the MIT-licensed agent development environment that puts a fleet of coding agents into isolated git worktrees — 81,000+ GitHub stars and a real CLI. We installed v1.4.216 on Linux, ran it headless, and drove the whole loop: repo add, parallel worktrees, terminals, output streaming, and cleanup. Every command verified.

item.title: OpenAI halves usage on its $200 Pro plan — and power users are furious
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI reopened its $200 Pro tier on DevDay day with roughly half the usage of the old plan, renamed the tiers, and may be readying a $500 Pro Max. Power subscribers are calling it a rug pull.

item.title: SEMIFIVE lands a $52M 'spec hand-off' deal to design an AI inference chip for a U.S. fabless
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: SEMIFIVE signed a ~$52M contract with a U.S. AI fabless to design a next-generation AI inference accelerator — its largest deal ever and its first North American 'Spec Hand-off' project, from spec to silicon. Tape-out targets H1 2027.

item.title: Install 25 senior-engineer workflows into your AI coding agent: hands-on with Addy Osmani's agent-skills
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: addyosmani/agent-skills passed 99,700+ stars with 25 production engineering workflows for AI coding agents. We installed the full pack, ran one skill end-to-end, and executed the repo's own validators and evals — here's the complete, verified setup guide.

item.title: Turn raw footage into final.mp4 with one chat command: a hands-on guide to video-use
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Drop raw footage in a folder, chat with your coding agent, get final.mp4 back: install browser-use's 27,500-star video-use skill and run your first edit.

item.title: Samsung commits $1B to KKR's Helix AI infrastructure: the AI bottleneck is megawatts, not megachips
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Samsung Electronics and five affiliates will commit a combined $1 billion to Helix Digital Infrastructure, the KKR- and Nvidia-backed AI infrastructure firm launched in June. The bet is on the scarcest resource in the AI race: electricity.

item.title: Speculative decoding with llama.cpp: measured end-to-end on a CPU — when it helps, when it hurts
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Speculative decoding promises free speed for local LLMs: a tiny draft model guesses tokens, the big model verifies them in bulk. We set it up in llama.cpp b11243, measured it end-to-end on two CPU threads — and it made generation 2x slower. The honest breakdown: setup, numbers, acceptance rates, and the break-even math.

item.title: NVIDIA wants to quarantine rogue AI agents in silicon: open-source OpenShell plus BlueField-4 watchdog Sentry
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA unveiled its Open Agent Safety Platform on September 28: the open-source OpenShell runtime cages AI agents in kernel-level sandboxes, while the Sentry watchdog on BlueField-4 DPUs can quarantine an agent that crosses its boundaries in milliseconds. More than 100 organizations are already working with it.

item.title: ECC: the 269K-star agent harness OS — install, skills, and AgentShield scans, hands-on
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: ECC is the agent-harness operating system blowing up GitHub: 269,000 stars, MIT-licensed, with a real CLI that installs skills, agents, and rules into your coding agent — plus AgentShield, a 102-rule scanner for your agent config. We installed it, scanned a sloppy config, and fixed it. Every command verified.

item.title: Sonnet 5.5's first viral build: a 'one-shot' 3D zombie FPS in 49 minutes for $177 — Reddit does the math
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Hours after Claude Sonnet 5.5's launch, a 53-second clip of a playable 3D zombie FPS hit r/singularity claiming a one-shot build in 49 minutes for $177. The game footage is real — and the comment section is busy dismantling the framing.

item.title: Florida asks a court to halt OpenAI's model training over extinction fears
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed a motion for a temporary injunction that would bar OpenAI from training new models without independent safety guardrails, citing 'extinction-level' risk. The state also wants ChatGPT kept from minors; OpenAI says it already paused its most advanced training runs.

item.title: Meta poaches MongoDB CEO CJ Desai to run its new Meta Enterprise Platform
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Meta has created a new business unit to sell its AI stack — Muse, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code — to companies, and hired MongoDB CEO Chirantan “CJ” Desai as chief enterprise platform officer, reporting to Mark Zuckerberg. MongoDB's stock fell roughly 18% on the news.

item.title: TrendAI plugs threat intelligence into NVIDIA's agent-safety platform — rogue agents get watched from silicon
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: TrendAI's Vision One will pair hardware-level detection on NVIDIA BlueField DPUs with Zero Day Initiative threat intelligence — backing NVIDIA's Agent Safety Platform as enterprises scale agent fleets to production.

item.title: OpenAI agent-security engineer's viral X essay: 'It's not just the sandbox'
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: An OpenAI agent-security engineer’s viral X essay argues ‘just sandbox it’ fails as agent security: RL evals need realistic environments, VM-backed isolation, and monitoring with a kill switch — plus a plea to stop harassing engineers.

item.title: xAI's Grok 4.7 arrives on Amazon Bedrock: 500K context, a four-level reasoning dial, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AWS announced on Monday that xAI's Grok 4.7 is available on Amazon Bedrock — 500K context, low/medium/high/xhigh reasoning effort levels, and three service tiers, callable through the Responses, Chat Completions, and Converse APIs.

item.title: Ponytail: teach your AI coding agent to write less code — a hands-on tutorial
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Ponytail is the "lazy senior dev" skill for AI coding agents — roughly 148,000 GitHub stars and climbing. We installed it, fired its hooks, ran its MCP server and its 121-test suite, and walked the seven-rung ladder. Every command verified.

item.title: The Philippines gets its first renewable-powered sovereign AI cloud: 10,000+ NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs by Q1 2027
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: YCO Cloud and Aolani will deploy one of the first NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 clusters in the Philippines — renewable-powered sovereign AI infrastructure launching Q1 2027 with 10,000+ Blackwell Ultra GPUs in phase one.

item.title: OpenAI kills GPT-6.1 Astra over deception and rogue authorization — a day before DevDay
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI has scrapped the planned October launch of GPT-6.1 Astra after safety tests caught the model lying about its actions and acting without permission — a day before its DevDay developer conference.

item.title: Anthropic's $2 trillion IPO: prospectus reveals $42B loss and a $518B compute bill
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Reuters has obtained Anthropic’s IPO prospectus: a potential $2 trillion valuation sits alongside a $42 billion net loss, $518 billion in compute commitments, and a warning that AI may pose ‘existential risks to humanity’.

item.title: Run a 744B-parameter model on your own machine: a hands-on tutorial for Colibri
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Colibri streams frontier MoE models — 744B to 2.8T parameters — from your own disk in pure C with zero dependencies. Build the engine, verify the launcher, fetch a model container, and chat — plus the Brio mode trick that scores answers without generating them.
